blocks.text: This chapter does not treat monarchy as simply good or simply evil. The people’s request is granted, yet Samuel’s warning and the LORD’s words make clear that both king and people remain accountable to the LORD. The chapter also cautions against reading Israel’s lack of a king as, by itself, an endorsement of every form of monarchy.

The chapters that follow preserve a deliberate tension: Israel’s request is severely criticized here, while Saul is later selected and empowered. Read together, 1 Samuel 8–12 presents monarchy as permitted, but accountable within Israel’s covenant life, rather than as wholly approved or wholly condemned.
